Monocular Drone-Camera Range Prediction

A compact depth model. A causal update policy.
An evidence-based study of accuracy and compute.

speaker_notes: Introduce the team after replacing the title-slide placeholders. AeroDepth-Lite predicts dense Euclidean camera range in metres and evaluates causal inference scheduling. This deck follows the supplied 13-slide outline. It summarizes existing saved research; no experiment was rerun. Source: docs/FINAL_REPORT.md. Evidence current to 29 October 2026.

text: How can a small drone estimate scene range while limiting repeated inference?

Recover dense metric range from
monocular RGB under changing
terrain, weather and visibility.

A fresh model call for every frame
adds work. Reusing an old map can
increase staleness and miss scene
changes.

Average error can
hide near errors

Overall gains may coexist with worse
errors below 10 m. Model calls,
update delay and measured time all
matter.
Evaluate compact range prediction and causal scheduling together, including near-field regressions and real timing.
speaker_notes: The gap is the integration and evaluation question addressed by this project, not a claim that no previous work studied efficient depth. Practical motivation is limited compute on small UAV platforms. This project uses simulation and does not demonstrate flight safety, obstacle detection or battery savings. Source: docs/FINAL_REPORT.md, Problem and objectives; Limitations and conclusion.

speaker_notes: Project-specific contributions: implement a compact positive metric-range decoder, integrate a causal scheduler, perform controlled A/KD experiments, preserve rejected-teacher and negative-KD evidence, and publish reproducible inference/evaluation artifacts with a local dashboard. MobileNetV3, ResNet, MidAir and distillation are prior work. The scheduler risk cache is verified to preserve decisions and reduces scheduler overhead, but does not show a robust end-to-end gain. Individual team responsibilities were not supplied, so no personal contribution is invented. Source: docs/FINAL_REPORT.md.

text: Preserve the range target and keep related flight paths in one split.
Match RGB, range and sensor records using the frozen allowlist.
Reinterpret PNG bits as float16 range. Keep finite GT in [0.1, 1000] m.

Full-frame 192 × 320; bilinear RGB; nearest target / mask; ImageNet
normalization once.
Paired horizontal flip for RGB, target and mask; no validation augmentation.
Group weather variants of a path; quarantine legacy tests; select on validation only; keep current GT out of scheduler decisions.
speaker_notes: Invalid depth values are replaced by zero only after creating the valid-pixel mask, then excluded from losses and metrics. Near field is valid ground-truth range <10 m. No crop or learned scale correction; softplus+0.1 has no upper prediction clamp. Feature extraction is learned by the encoder; there is no separate handcrafted feature selection for the depth network. Weather-equivalent paths identified using position-stream hashes stay grouped. Different paths may share scenery, so geographic isolation is not established. Validation was used repeatedly for development and model selection. Current GT range and privileged true velocity do not enter V2 decisions. Sources: docs/FINAL_REPORT.md; docs/expanded_training.md; results/expanded_preparation_20261026/dataset_contract.json.

text: Causal runtime workflow · drawn with editable shapes and connectors
First frame: infer. Maximum reuse age: 4 frames.

GT range is used for offline
scoring only.
speaker_notes: Diagram consists of ordinary editable PowerPoint shapes and arrow connectors; no image-generation model was used. Runtime: resize current RGB; scheduler computes change versus last inferred RGB and combines causal simulated IMU/GPS, last predicted risk and age; infer updates cached prediction, otherwise reuse the prior map without warping. The model normalizes RGB internally exactly once (the preprocessing box denotes the full transform contract). State resets at path boundaries. Risk cache is refreshed only on fresh-source token/reset. Ground truth is used offline, never as a decision input. Source: docs/FINAL_REPORT.md and implementation. Teacher/KD is training-only, not on this inference path.

Why selected: compact ImageNet-initialized encoder with a

A / KD: 10 epochs each; selected epoch 9
Teacher B: 20 epochs; selected epoch 3

Student LR 10⁻⁴ · weight decay 10⁻⁴
Cosine minimum: 10⁻⁶
Teacher encoder / decoder LR: 10⁻⁵ / 10⁻⁴
Loss = L1 range + 0.2 L1 log-range + 0.1 gradient L1 | KD adds 0.2 log-range consistency
speaker_notes: Tools: Python, PyTorch, torchvision, NumPy, Pillow, h5py, Matplotlib and Streamlit. Hardware recorded: GTX 1650 (4 GB) for training; CPU/CUDA timing was measured separately. Original student completed 50 epochs on 17,635 training frames and selected epoch 4 by recorded AMP validation AbsRel. A and exploratory KD independently start from identical original epoch-4 weights and BN buffers with fresh matched optimizer/scheduler/scaler/RNG state. Their common dataset is expanded 44,098 training frames; final comparisons use FP32 validation. A and KD selected epoch 9 by minimum pooled FP32 validation AbsRel. Teacher is ImageNet1K_V2 initialized ResNet-50 V1.5, selected epoch 3; it failed the near-field acceptance gate. During exploratory KD it is frozen, eval mode, FP32, no-grad, and sees the same augmented image as the student. Near loss weight is zero. KD adds 0.2 masked absolute log-range consistency on valid training pixels. No classification-logit temperature KD is used. Sources: docs/FINAL_REPORT.md; configs and frozen launch copies. Numerical AMP recovery preserves update accounting and retries rather than silently skipping steps.

text: 4,410 validation frames · lower error is better · identical evaluation masks
Teacher B failed its acceptance gate: Kite near RMSE 6.636 m vs A 4.695 m.
Higher near RMSE · A vs original
δ1 = fraction with max(prediction / GT, GT / prediction) < 1.25. Classification precision, recall, F1 and confusion matrix do not apply.
speaker_notes: AbsRel = mean(|P−GT|/GT); RMSE = sqrt(sum((P−GT)^2)/valid-pixel count). Values are pooled by additive pixel sums, not averaged per-frame RMSE. Valid GT is finite in [0.1,1000] m; near GT <10 m. All three models have 212,903,814 valid and 32,267,840 near pixels. A improves overall RMSE by 5.80% and AbsRel by 11.84% vs original, but near RMSE worsens 16.18%. Original and A differ in training data and budget, so this does not isolate an architecture effect. KD vs A is a matched one-seed comparison; KD pooled AbsRel is 1.59% worse and near RMSE 1.42% worse. Teacher B failed the gate: Kite foggy near RMSE 6.636090 m vs A 4.695176 m. The exploratory rejected-teacher run does not show that all distillation fails. No confidence interval, multi-seed statistical claim, independent new-test result or cross-paper benchmark superiority is available. Source: comparison.csv and docs/FINAL_REPORT.md.

text: Experimental results: scheduling and measured cost
Supervised A on validation · policy parameters frozen before this comparison

Lower pooled near RMSE than fixed
budget at equal total calls.

Overall error slightly worsens; max
event-update delay rises.
Actual timing · 256-frame stress windows · median end-to-end seconds

Risk caching reduced scheduler time by 13.43%
on CPU and 15.81% on GPU.
No robust end-to-end speedup was measured.
speaker_notes: ¹ Delay is in camera frames and refers to time until a prediction update after an offline-defined event, NOT obstacle-detection accuracy. Near RMSE V2 vs fixed budget: 9.14% lower pooled, but Kite near RMSE is slightly worse and PLE improves. V2 uses 905/1551 calls across Kite/PLE; budget fixed uses 1228/1228. Total calls coincide, not per-path calls. V2 overall AbsRel 0.268088 vs fixed 0.267810; max delay 2 vs 1. Visual ablation changes budget and state trajectory, so it is not an equal-compute causal estimate. Timing uses two fixed 128-frame windows, 3 repetitions/device, FP32 batch 1, CPU 2 threads, 10 excluded warmups. In these windows every-frame/fixed-budget/V2 each make 256/144/222 calls per run, unlike the full-path validation call budgets. CPU median [min,max] seconds: every 10.4203 [10.2725,14.3289], budget 8.6725 [8.3859,9.1672], cached V2 10.4290 [10.1152,10.6138]. CUDA: every 9.0176 [8.8663,9.4765], budget 7.8625 [7.7724,8.3073], cached V2 8.7650 [8.7047,9.3071]. Risk caching vs uncached improves scheduler median 13.43% CPU /15.81% GPU; end-to-end CPU is 3.07% worse and GPU 0.37% better with overlapping repetition ranges. Model-only latency is not complete throughput. No energy or battery benefit was measured.

Two familiar validation paths; correlated frames; synthetic

regression.

and real-flight transfer.

Supervised A improves overall range prediction, while near-field error worsens.
Exploratory KD underperforms A; adaptive scheduling offers a mixed quality / cost trade-off.
speaker_notes: Reserved independent final study: NOT RUN because 8 image/depth streams are unavailable; sensor metadata alone is insufficient. The older 4,436-frame test belongs to the historical original-model study and is quarantined, not evidence for new-model generalization. Future work is proposed, not completed: acquisition and integrity checks, a frozen independent protocol, multi-seed replication, near-field loss/coverage experiments, real drone sensor latency and power measurements. Teacher-regression mechanisms are hypotheses; the separate gradient probe did not justify repair. No measured energy saving, battery gain, flight safety or guaranteed obstacle detection is claimed. Finish with supported findings and invite questions. Sources: docs/FINAL_REPORT.md and acquisition inventory.
